text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - Leading British shares ended a dull session firmer on Monday, marking a second consecutive closing high, but trading volume was thin with many dealing rooms half-empty ahead of the Christmas holiday. The FTSE 100 added 9.6 points to settle at 4,087.2, the day's high, on turnover of only 452.5 million shares.

FRANKFURT - German shares limped their way to a lower close in thinly traded floor dealings on Monday -- the last day before a three-day Christmas break. The 30-share DAX index dropped 8.88 points to end at 2,845.57, after hovering in a range of just seven points. In post-bourse trade the index was up 8.55 at 2,844.09.

PARIS - French shares closed slightly higher on Monday after having spent most of the day in the red, following afternoon support by a higher Wall Street market. The U.S. markets were boosted by the November personal income data. Paris had suffered earlier from profit-taking on the last day of the December account The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 8.91 points or 0.39 percent at 2,287.44 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,296.5 from 2,280 on Friday's close.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed lower in thin volumes as Novartis, the newly created world number two in pharmaceuticals, ended its first day of trading below opening levels. The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) was down 14.6 points, or 0.38 percent, to 3,875.5. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended off 6.46 points, or 0.26 percent, at 2,475.22 points.

TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market is closed on Monday for a national holiday. The market will reopen on Tuesday. On Friday, the key Nikkei 225 average closed 119.79 points or 0.61 percent higher at 19,690.46 after see-sawing in positive and negative territory towards the close. But its March futures lost 70 points to close at 19,590.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks bounded ahead to close sharply higher, with buying fueled by the recent turnaround on Wall Street and an improved outlook for the local real estate market. The Hang Seng Index closed 200.07 points higher at 13,331.48 after touching a high of 13,361.24.

SYDNEY - Australian shares edged to a slightly higher close on Monday with light buying interest in the bank sector supporting the market as it wound down for the Christmas break. The All Ordinaries index closed 6.7 points higher at 2,380.5, not far from its intra-day high of 2,384.7.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended slightly down on a Monday marked by quiet trade ahead of the looming seasonal festivities. With about 350 million rands worth of shares changing hands trade was dull and prices drifted downwards in the absence of any clear direction from other markets. The all-share index dipped 4.0 points to 6,536.4 as industrials shed 26.8 points to end at 7,769.0.
